entry.title: Agent Anomaly Detection: Safeguarding agents across other clouds | Google Developers Blog
entry.summary: Agent Anomaly Detection now monitors ADK agents running across AWS, Azure, or on-premises by analyzing their traces and logs in your Google Cloud project. By ingesting OpenTelemetry-formatted data thr
entry.content: Agent Anomaly Detection now monitors ADK agents running across AWS, Azure, or on-premises by analyzing their traces and logs in your Google Cloud project. By ingesting OpenTelemetry-formatted data through the Telemetry API, it evaluates full conversations for behavioral drift without needing access to the agent's underlying runtime. This enables security teams to detect risks like rogue behaviors, tool misuse, and resource exhaustion across multi-cloud environments.

entry.summary: Semantic governance policies enable developers to govern AI agents by evaluating every proposed tool call inline before execution. Operating via Agent Gateway, the policy engine checks each action aga
entry.content: Semantic governance policies enable developers to govern AI agents by evaluating every proposed tool call inline before execution. Operating via Agent Gateway, the policy engine checks each action against user intent and plain-language rules to prevent unauthorized data sharing and prompt injection attacks. Developers can easily attach natural-language constraints to their agents and monitor auditable verdicts through Cloud Logging.

entry.title: How to handle user, connector, and agent auth in Gemini Enterprise with a custom UI | Google Developers Blog
entry.summary: When building a custom enterprise UI on top of Gemini Enterprise's :streamAssist API, developers must manually implement three core authentication layers. These include authenticating users or workloa
entry.content: When building a custom enterprise UI on top of Gemini Enterprise's :streamAssist API, developers must manually implement three core authentication layers. These include authenticating users or workloads via Google Identity or Workforce/Workload Identity Federation, managing third-party 3-legged OAuth (3LO) for Federated Connectors through the Keystore, and configuring on-demand per-tool OAuth for custom ADK agents using Vertex AI Agent Engine and GCP Auth Manager.

entry.content: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. entry.title: Distributed LLM Training Across Metros: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText | Google Developers Blog
entry.summary: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText enables developers to efficiently train large language models across geographically distributed TPU slices by streaming parameter fragments instead of synchronizing full mo
entry.content: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText enables developers to efficiently train large language models across geographically distributed TPU slices by streaming parameter fragments instead of synchronizing full models at every step. This approach slashes cross-slice communication volume by over 60× and eliminates network stalls, allowing seamless multi-datacenter scaling without degrading model convergence or quality.

entry.title: Agents are sessions, not requests: size GKE node pools for AI agent sessions | Google Developers Blog
entry.summary: AI agent sessions remain active and idle for most of the workday, making traditional one-Pod-per-session allocations inefficient for cluster resources. By using open-source tools like Agent Substrate
entry.content: AI agent sessions remain active and idle for most of the workday, making traditional one-Pod-per-session allocations inefficient for cluster resources. By using open-source tools like Agent Substrate and AX on GKE, developers can park idle sessions in object storage to release compute resources while maintaining session state. This approach optimizes resource utilization and reduces Kubernetes node costs by up to 40%.

entry.title: TPU Model Design Considerations and Optimization Guide | Google Developers Blog
entry.summary: The newly launched AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-codesign guide provides hardware-grounded design rules to help developers maximize performance on TPUs for LLMs and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) workloads. Key prin
entry.content: The newly launched AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-codesign guide provides hardware-grounded design rules to help developers maximize performance on TPUs for LLMs and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) workloads. Key principles include aligning reduction and output dimensions to 256 for systolic arrays, adopting LatentMoE to compress routed token traffic, and mapping parallel axes directly onto physical links.
